name: Sphere Speed Lines
move: a glossy blue-violet sphere rolls in from the left trailing fine speed lines along the bottom of a light frame while a huge sentence builds word by word above it and the camera pans along the line, then the sphere speeds up and flies out right and the scene flips to dark
how: The sentence (Sharp Grotesk 400, set 1.7 frame widths wide, about 180 px, baseline at 57.6% of the height) sits in a world the camera pans 1.27 widths from 0.12 to 1.57 s on cubic-bezier(.55,.15,.625,1), so the full stop ends at 87.5% of the frame. A word lands every 0.233 s (7 frames) from 0.1 s: it pops in pale, rises 45 px (cubicOut 0.3 s) and darkens left to right (a grey-to-ink background-clip gradient swept over 0.36 s). The sphere is a 412 px disc lit from the upper right (radial #e6ebf7 to #2a3cb8) over a 1.14x, 34 px-blurred blue disc that sits 0.12R high and lags its screen motion by 20 ms, with motion blur above 2000 px/s. Path in frame units: x = .12 + .78 quartOut(s/1.1) + .32 s + 1.2 (s-1.5)^2.5, y drops .5 to .87 (quartOut over 0.6 s) and later rises by 1.1 (s-1.85)^1.6: a fast arrival that lands on the floor, rolls slower than the camera (drifting back to the left of frame), then accelerates up and out. Speed lines: five 2.2 px grey strokes on a canvas, each the sphere's own last 1.1 s of path ending under it, heads 70 ms apart; the fan is wide while it drops and near-parallel once it rolls, and the lines catch up from 0.27 s. Text the sphere passes under turns pale and recovers behind it (a mask: wash = e^(-d/0.13W) of the distance behind the sphere). From 1.95 s the floor floods blue; at 2.36 s a hard flip to a black-to-navy ground, held to 3 s.
adapt: SENTENCE is the spoken line and WORD_EVERY should follow its word timings; colours are .stage tokens (--ground, --ground-low, --floor, --ink, --ghost, --orb-1..6, --night, --night-low). Keep the line about 1.7 widths long so the camera has to pan while the sphere rolls under it; a shorter sentence means less pan (CAM_END is derived from the set width).
port: Custom shot type js/shots/sphere-line.js. The sentence belongs in the film's captions (spoken words): the shot reads it from s, splits it into words and lands word i at its caption time instead of every 0.233 s. animate(el, s, D) returns a timeline tweening a proxy {t: 0 to 3} drawn in ShotKit.frameHook with this page's seek(t) scoped to el (the speed lines are a canvas). The flip at 2.36 s is the join to a dark next shot; drop it otherwise and end on the sphere's exit.
caveats: The reel's face is wider than Sharp Grotesk, so the words sit a little narrower and smaller
Speed lines are path history, so they follow any path you give the sphere; the reel's exit lines rise a touch steeper
The last 0.64 s is the dark ground the next scene starts on
